findings.passage: "Lord, have mercy on our children," said Rep. Davis. "Once again, our children and teachers suffer through another mass shooting in Tennessee. The shooter was reported to have two 'AR-style weapons.' As a veteran who supports the Second Amendment, time is overdue to limit access to wartime 'AR-style' assault weapons. We must put the safety of our children first."
findings.note: Statement issued by the House Media Services Office in her name after the Nashville school shooting.

findings.passage: We must stand with these legislators and for gun safety reform.
findings.note: Statement in her name in a joint release on the Tennessee expulsions; she also says she is a veteran and supporter of the Second Amendment. The release says Reps. Davis, Scott and Schofield introduced a 2023 gun-violence package, listing bills on reporting lost or stolen guns, safe storage, selling assault weapons to under-21s, rapid-fire devices and a public-health resolution.

findings.passage: As a veteran who supports the Second Amendment, I believe we can balance the rights of gun owners with the need to protect the public from acts of gun violence.
findings.note: Statement in her name after the Midtown Atlanta shooting. In the same sentence group she says lawmakers need to prioritize gun safety reform. The release lists HB 4, HB 553 (extreme-risk orders), HB 224, HB 366, HB 554, HB 555 and HR 56 as the package being amplified by Reps. Scott, Davis, Burnough and Schofield.

findings.passage: As a legislator, I understand that there is no single piece of legislation that can eliminate senseless shootings.
